                    ### Question
                    During a study on the immune system, an investigator isolates and labels T cells from the cortex of the thymus. The T cells that do not bind cortical epithelial cells expressing MHC molecules undergo apoptosis within 3–4 days. Which of the following best describes the T cells during this phase of differentiation?

                    ### Options
                    opa. CD4+ and CD8+
opb. Th2
opc. CD8+
opd. T cell precursor
ope. CD4+

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
During their development in the thymus cortex, T cells express both CD4 and CD8 markers, categorizing them as double-positive. These cells must bind to cortical epithelial cells presenting MHC molecules to survive and differentiate. Failure to bind leads to apoptosis through negative selection. This process ensures that only T cells capable of recognizing self-MHC molecules mature into functional immune cells. Relevant evidence supports the critical role of MHC interactions in this selection process.
